nodes.referent: The metaphysical doctrine/position holding that reality is fundamentally constituted by processes, events, and becoming rather than by static, self-subsistent substances -- associated primarily with Alfred North Whitehead's philosophy of organism as systematized in Process and Reality (1929), and developed further by Charles Hartshorne and later process theologians. This is NOT the looser, perennial 'process approach' sometimes traced back to Heraclitus's flux doctrine or to Bergson's duree (SEP names Heraclitus as the founder of that older, broader approach, a different and prior lineage); NOT process theology specifically (the theological application of this metaphysics to the concept of God, a narrower downstream topic); and NOT a claim that a single, formally bounded 'school' with fixed membership and a named founder exists -- SEP's own Process Philosophy entry states the field 'is not tied to any school, method, position, or even paradigmatic notion of process.' The referent intended here is the specific, bounded 20th-century Whiteheadian doctrine as indexed by philosophy reference taxonomies (e.g. PhilPapers' Metaphysics > Global Metaphysical Theories > Process Philosophy category), not the more diffuse field-level or perennial-tradition reading.

nodes.referent: Charles Hartshorne (1897-2000), American philosopher and theologian who taught at the University of Chicago, Emory University, and the University of Texas at Austin; principal developer of process theology by extending Alfred North Whitehead's process philosophy into a systematic theistic metaphysics (neoclassical/panentheistic conception of God), co-editor (with Paul Weiss) of the early volumes of Charles Sanders Peirce's Collected Papers, and a defender of a modal version of the ontological argument. This is specifically the 20th-century American process philosopher/theologian born 1897 and died 2000 -- not any other person sharing the surname Hartshorne, and not the year 2003 sometimes seen misattributed as his death year.
nodes.source_hint: English Wikipedia -- 'Charles Hartshorne' article (oldid 1359826539, per this order's verified quote): 'Hartshorne is also noted for developing Alfred North Whitehead's process philosophy into process theology.' Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy (IEP) -- 'Process Philosophy' entry (per this order's verified quote): 'the term "process philosophy" is primarily associated with the work of the philosophers Alfred North Whitehead (1861-1947) and Charles Hartshorne (1897-2000).'
